title: Detection and Quantification of Nanoparticle-Induced Intracellular ROS in Live Cells by Laser Scanning Confocal Microscopy.
markdown:
## Protocol: Protocol for detection and quantification of nanoparticle-induced intracellular reactive oxygen species in live cells by laser-scanning confocal microscopy

### Overview

This protocol outlines the procedure for detecting and quantifying nanoparticle-induced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) in live HT1080 cells using laser-scanning confocal microscopy. The process involves preparing specific reagent solutions, seeding and treating cells with nanoparticles or controls, and performing live-cell imaging under controlled environmental conditions to ensure cell viability and image quality.

### Materials/Reagents

- DPBS (Dulbecco's Phosphate-Buffered Saline)
- Sterile deionized water
- RPMI 1640 medium supplemented with 2.0 mM L-glutamine, 1 vol% penicillin/streptomycin, and 10 vol% FBS
- H2DCFDA stock solution (40 mM)
- Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) stock solution (30% w/w)
- Refractive index matching oil (37 °C)

### Equipment

- Glass-bottom imaging dish
- Incubator system (with CO2 supply or alternative buffering)
- Laser-scanning confocal microscope with live-cell imaging chamber
- Zen Black software
- Lens cleaning tissue

### Safety & Sterility

Maintain sterile conditions during reagent preparation and cell handling. Use warm DPBS (37 °C) for washing steps to minimize thermal shock. Ensure the incubator system is equilibrated prior to imaging to maintain physiological conditions.

## Reagent Preparation

### Pre-experiment Setup

1. Prepare a 5 µM H2DCFDA solution by diluting the 40 mM stock solution with DPBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare a 0.01 µM H2O2 solution by diluting the 30% w/w H2O2 stock solution with sterile deionized water. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->

## Cell Culture and Treatment

### Day 0: Cell Seeding

1. Seed HT1080 cells at a density of 1 × 10^6 in a glass-bottom imaging dish and allow them to grow for 24 hours in RPMI 1640 medium containing 2.0 mM L-glutamine, 1 vol% penicillin/streptomycin, and 10 vol% FBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->

### NP Treatment Branch

1. Treat the cells with nanoparticles at a concentration of 400 μg/mL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->
2. After 8 hours of treatment, gently wash the cells with warm DPBS (37 °C) for approximately 30 seconds. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S02 -->
3. Treat the cells with 100 µL of 5 µM H2DCFDA and incubate for 30 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S03 -->
4. Pipette 500 µL of RPMI 1640 media onto the cells to maintain cell viability throughout the imaging process. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S04 -->

### Untreated Control Branch

#### Branch A: Untreated Control

1. For the untreated control branch, treat the cells solely with H2DCFDA as an intracellular ROS-detecting probe. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->

### Positive Control Branch

#### Branch B: Positive Control

1. For the positive control branch, incubate the cells for 1 hour in a freshly prepared 0.01 mM hydrogen peroxide solution derived from the 30% w/w stock solution. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S01 -->

### General Constraint

> **Operational constraint:** Ensure all samples are prepared and tested separately, not contiguously. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S01 -->

## Microscopy Imaging

### Imaging Setup

1. Allow the incubator system to equilibrate for 2 hours. If CO2 is unavailable, supply the cell media with 10-20 mM HEPES. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
2. Open the microscope live-cell imaging chamber and clean the objective lens with lens cleaning tissue. If using an immersion lens, add a drop of 37 °C refractive index matching oil to minimize scattering and improve point spread function uniformity. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->
3. Place the sample in the sample holder of the microscope stage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->
4. Open Zen Black software and wait until all hardware is initialized. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S04 -->

### Acquisition Parameters

1. Adjust the lens focus until the cellular midplane is visible through the eyepiece. Explore the sample with the joystick until the cell of interest is located for imaging. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S01 -->
2. Adjust imaging parameters in the Acquisition menu in the software for the sample point spread function, setting the pixel size to approximately 0.1 µm. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S02 -->
3. Adjust display contrast using Best Fit or Min-Max in the Look-Up-Table (LUT) menu at the bottom of the screen. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S03 -->
4. To obtain unsaturated images while maintaining cell life and avoiding phototoxicity, adjust the Master gain to 883 for fluorescent signal detection (CH1) and to 228 for forward fluorescent probe and image saturation photomultiplier tube detection (NDD_T1) of the scattered signal to give a bright-field image. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S04 -->
5. Adjust laser intensity and scanner speed by setting the Pixel dwell time to 0.66 μs. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S05 -->
6. Ensure Nyquist sampling is fulfilled by setting the pixel size to 0.085 μm × 0.085 μm (Scaling X x Scaling Y), which is suitable for a lens numerical aperture of 1.4 (Objective). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S06 -->
7. Set the pinhole at 1 Airy unit (Position (x,y,z) - Position 1). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S07 -->
8. Set averaging at 4 lines (Average) to cancel out noise from images and amplify the signal-to-noise ratio. Perform this adjustment on the brightest sample first to ensure that other fainter samples do not saturate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T1-S08 -->

### Image Capture

1. Specify Live or Continuous settings in the relevant windows and capture images using the Snap tab. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S01 -->
2. Save images in Carl Zeiss Imaging (CZI) format or other imaging formats, preserving raw data without compression, depending on the microscope used, until further processing. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T2-S02 -->

## References
